metaData.originalTitle: 端侧 AI 提速 80%？如何让 Qwen3-VL 在手机起飞
metaData.title: 80% Speed Boost for On-Device AI? How to Make Qwen3-VL Fly on Your Phone
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a hands-on demonstration of how to leverage Arm SME2 instructions and the MNN inference engine to efficiently deploy the Qwen3-VL-4B multimodal model on flagship phones supporting SME2, achieving over 80% speedup in the Prefill phase.
metaData.summary: Written by an engineer from the Tongyi Lab, this article serves as a practical engineering tutorial for on-device AI developers. It focuses on the SME2 instruction set of the Armv9 architecture, explaining its principle of achieving efficient matrix multiplication through the ZA matrix accumulator. Using Alibaba's open-source MNN inference engine, the article details a complete deployment workflow: compiling from source (with SME2 support enabled), downloading and converting the model, verifying via command line, and building an Android application. It provides specific compilation commands, model deployment steps, and performance testing methods, presenting real-world test data from a vivo X300: 81% speedup in the Prefill phase and 13% speedup in the Decode phase. Finally, the article also covers advanced tuning methods for model export and runtime parameters.

mainPoints.point: The SME2 instruction set enables efficient matrix multiplication via the ZA matrix accumulator, a key acceleration technology for on-device AI inference.
mainPoints.explanation: Traditional Neon instructions require manual decomposition of matrix multiplication, whereas SME2 instructions like FMOPA can complete the outer product accumulation of a matrix tile in a single instruction, significantly boosting computational throughput, especially for compute-intensive tasks like Prefill.

mainPoints.point: The MNN inference engine adopts a 'compile-time built-in + runtime auto-detection' design for SME2, requiring no manual configuration from developers.
mainPoints.explanation: The compile flag `-DMNN_SME2=ON` controls whether to include SME2-optimized kernels. At runtime, it automatically detects hardware support: if available, it uses the accelerated path; if not, it gracefully falls back, ensuring compatibility.

mainPoints.point: SME2 acceleration provides significant gains for the Prefill phase (+81%) but limited gains for the Decode phase (+13%).
mainPoints.explanation: Prefill is a compute-intensive task (large batch matrix multiplications) that can fully leverage SME2's advantages. Decode generates tokens one by one, where the bottleneck is memory bandwidth, limiting SME2's benefits.

mainPoints.point: The article provides a complete end-to-end on-device deployment path, including engine compilation, model preparation, command-line verification, and app building.
mainPoints.explanation: The tutorial covers the entire process from setting up the Android NDK environment to installing the final APK, providing specific command-line examples and performance testing tools for high operability.

keyQuotes: SME2, as Arm's latest matrix acceleration instruction set, delivers tangible performance improvements for on-device large model inference through deep integration with MNN—achieving over 80% speedup in the Prefill phase.
MNN's support for SME2 adopts a compile-time built-in plus runtime auto-detection design, requiring no manual configuration from users.

relatedArticles.title: Qwen3.7-Max Redefines the Foundation of AI Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Alibaba Tongyi Lab releases Qwen3.7-Max, demonstrating long-horizon agent stability in extreme stress tests with 35 hours of continuous autonomous execution and 1,158 tool calls without interruption, achieving cross-framework generalization through a decoupled training architecture.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: 215 SOTA Benchmarks + Emergent Vibe Coding! Qwen3.5-Omni Released
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab releases Qwen3.5-Omni, a native omni-modal large model that achieves SOTA in 215 benchmarks, supporting real-time audio-visual interaction, voice cloning, and emergent Vibe Coding capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: Qwen3.6-Plus: A Major Leap in Coding Agent Capabilities!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Qwen-Lab releases Qwen3.6-Plus, focusing on strengthening the stable execution of Coding Agents, with support for a 1M context window and deep multimodal reasoning.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: Can AI Write Code in Truly "Mission-Critical" Backend Systems?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article shares the complete methodology—Harness Engineering—practiced by Tencent's CDN LEGO team for AI coding in ultra-large-scale, high-reliability backend systems. Through a five-layer architecture, three key levers (context, constraints, feedback), and multi-model adversarial code review, they built an engineering system that enables AI to safely and controllably produce high-quality code.

relatedArticles.title: From Transparent Development to Systems Engineering: AgentScope 2.0 Released
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: AgentScope 2.0 upgrades from transparent development to systems engineering, focusing on stable operation, security control, and production-level deployment capabilities for agents in real-world scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: All-in-One Text, Image, and Video! An Open-Source Framework for Multimodal Knowledge Bases
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab has open-sourced the VimRAG framework, which leverages Dynamic Acyclic Graphs (DAG) and Graph-Guided Policy Optimization to solve cross-modal retrieval and long-context reasoning challenges in mixed-media knowledge bases.

relatedArticles.title: A Practical Guide to 'Progressive Spec' for AI Coding in 2026
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes a 'Progressive Spec' framework for AI coding environments, leveraging structured documentation to drive AI collaboration and balance development standards with execution efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: Rethinking Development Infrastructure: When Agents Become First-Class Citizens
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes a unified framework of 'intent-driven + code precipitation', arguing that agents do not change the fundamental structure of software evolution but compress the 'intent → code' cycle from months/weeks to minutes, and thus deduces that development infrastructure must shift from People-Oriented to Agent-Oriented design principles.
